title: Maintenance, connected
subtitle: Project review & future implementation roadmap
body:
A garment-factory CMMS connecting machines, maintenance teams, spare parts and management.

WORKING-TREE REVIEW / 21 NOVEMBER 2026

Current capabilities, architecture, findings and a proposed implementation plan.

MAINTENANCE MODULE CMMS
01020304
ASSET → WORK ORDER → REPAIR → HISTORY
notes: Review includes uncommitted work. No live deployment, customer counts, business savings or security certification were established. Illustrations are conceptual, not screenshots.

title: One operational record for the floor
subtitle: Three needs connect the project
body:
01

Locate the asset

Track machine identity, unit, zone, production line and station.

02

Organize the work

Report faults, assign technicians, schedule PPM and follow workshop repairs.

03

Explain the outcome

Connect repair activity, parts used, recorded costs and maintenance history.
notes: Faster reporting, clearer ownership and better traceability are intended benefits. No measured downtime or cost reduction was supplied.

title: Breakdown to repair completion
subtitle: Ticket state connects reporting, ownership and recovery
body:
01

Report

Machine, fault details and urgency

02

Assign

Technician and dispatch

03

Attend

Start work and record repair activity

04

Complete

Action, parts, duration and proof

PENDING → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED
REJECTED is also supported.
notes: The client also supports stopping work. Completion can set a machine ACTIVE. Physical workshop return uses the machine movement workflow.

title: Service-station handover is transactional
subtitle: A strong pattern exists for coordinated updates
body:
ONE MONGODB TRANSACTION

01

Repair ticket

Save the service mechanic, due date and handover instructions.

02

Machine location

Move into the workshop and set UNDER_MAINTENANCE.

03

Asset log

Record the actor, time, destination and repair context.

Concurrent ticket or machine changes reject the handover rather than leaving a partial transfer.
notes: Requires Atlas or a MongoDB replica set. Default repair due date is ten calendar days ahead in India. The transaction guarantee applies to service transfer, not all stock and repair operations.

title: PPM scheduling is already implemented
subtitle: Schedules represent planned and completed preventive work
body:
01

Plan

Weekly, Monthly and 6-Month types; configurable interval, due date and assignee.

02

Execute

Start, stop and complete tasks with duration, technician notes and optional proof.

03

Review

Filter by due state, machine, line, category and technician.

Gap: task-level scheduling is not a structured per-check monthly inspection history.
notes: Completion updates lastServiced and nextDue. Test recurring tasks and due-state handling end to end: a record can retain COMPLETED while a future nextDue is stored.

title: Reports make activity reviewable
subtitle: History, T&A and reminders serve different needs
body:
01

History and costs

Machine dossiers, personnel records, status activity and recorded maintenance spending.

02

T&A reporting

Combined breakdown and PPM views for today, week, month or custom dates; PDF and Excel exports.

03

Reminder center

Breakdowns, overdue PPM, overdue service repairs, stock needs and other pending work.

Reminder popups run in the browser. They are not an always-on background escalation service.
notes: Reports include IST timestamps, technician, location, status and downtime. Exports use jsPDF/autotable and xlsx. No financial or utilization gains are claimed.

title: Company isolation starts with the session
subtitle: The server chooses a database through the registry
body:
01

Sign in

Resolve an account and issue a signed session

02

Check

Verify token and requested company

03

Resolve

Load the registered company database

04

Validate

Recheck active status and current role

Implemented: signed sessions, bcrypt support, HttpOnly session cookies and cross-company mismatch rejection.

Exception: public QR endpoints resolve company + asset without the normal signed session path.
notes: verifyPassword retains a legacy plaintext fallback. Tokens expire after 30 days. Public QR supports label reads, fault reporting and supported line moves. Its access model needs an explicit threat review; not every API requires login.

title: What works well in the design
subtitle: The model reflects real maintenance workflows
body:
01

Operational detail

Workshop handovers, custody, due dates, parts use and production locations are represented.

02

Tenant-aware foundation

Dedicated company databases, active account checks and scoped browser preferences support multiple workspaces.

03

Reviewable records

Asset logs, history, reports, imports and focused regression scripts support traceability.

Reuse the service-transfer transaction and focused domain helpers as implementation patterns.
notes: Architectural strengths inferred from source, not proof that all workflows have passed live user acceptance.

title: Resolve these gaps before wider rollout
subtitle: Specific findings from the current source
body:
PriorityFindingProposed correction
P0Broad update objects in general PATCH routesValidate fields, actor scope and state transitions on the server
P0Repair, machine and stock writes span requestsUse transaction-safe completion and stock issue with idempotency
P1Default rates can become stored repair valuesSeparate actual costs from estimates; require costing inputs
P1Local changes can precede failed server writesReconcile or roll back; refetch authoritative records
P1Legacy passwords and public QR writes widen exposureMigrate old hashes; control and monitor public actions
notes: Code findings, not tested exploits. Repair costing includes ₹250 missing-part and ₹350 hourly labor defaults. recordedMaintenanceCosts avoids invented amounts, but saved upstream values may include estimates. Add rate limits and consider signed QR tokens or authenticated writes.

title: Make QR the maintenance entry point
subtitle: Proposed: four clear actions after every scan
body:
▦
01

PPM

02

Breakdown

Fault details and urgency

03

Line relocation

Acceptance: preserve company and machine identity; retain origin, destination, actor and time for every move.
notes: The earlier four-choice component and structured PPM checklist are absent from the current checkout. This QR glyph is decorative. Validate receiving unit, zone, line and actor authority before transfer.

title: Digitize the paper PPM calendar
subtitle: Proposed: nine monthly checks and half-year oil service
body:
01Oil level
02Oil circulation
03Looper / hookset point
04Grease points
05Air leakage
06Safety guard
07Wheel cleaning
08Table cleaning & alignment
09Feed dog cleaning

OK / Needs attention / N/A
Mechanic · inspection date · notes · proof · reviewer

Oil service: January–June and July–December. Use machine-type templates and retain versioned history.
source: User-supplied Preventive Maintenance Calendar photo · src/types/cmms.ts PPMSchedule
notes: Propose checklist_templates, inspection_runs and inspection_results linked to machineId and scheduleId. Require N/A and failed-check reasons; create linked corrective tickets. Do not mark prior months complete based on the photo.

title: Make server commands authoritative
subtitle: Proposed: reliable maintenance updates
body:
01

Validate

Role, unit, fields, state and quantity

02

Commit

Ticket + stock + machine + audit together

03

Publish

Queue notifications after the commit

04

Reconcile

Return saved state and refresh the client

Acceptance: two technicians cannot issue the last spare twice; retrying a completion changes the data once.
source: Basis: src/lib/services/serviceRepairService.ts · current repair / parts APIs
notes: Use idempotency keys, optimistic concurrency/version checks, bounded stock updates and a stock-movement ledger. A transactional outbox supports notification retries and duplicate suppression. These are proposals.

title: Improve floor access and visibility
subtitle: Proposed enhancements after consistency work
body:
01

Offline mobile use

A PWA with a limited inspection queue, visible sync state and conflict resolution.

02

Server reminders

Background overdue jobs with retryable alerts and supervisor escalation.

03

Shared updates

Pagination, indexed search and targeted refresh; add SSE/WebSockets where measured latency warrants it.

Acceptance: users see what is saved, queued or conflicted; alerts continue with no dashboard open.
notes: Do not blindly queue stock deductions or cross-unit transfers offline. Cache only the active tenant’s required data. No delivery date is committed.

subtitle: Later-stage capabilities and prerequisites
body:
CapabilityPrerequisiteSuccess evidence
ERP / purchasing integrationStable part IDs, suppliers and stock ledgerApproved requests link to purchases and receipts
Condition monitoringSensor coverage, timestamps and machine mappingValidated thresholds and false-positive rates
Predictive maintenanceReliable failure, runtime and intervention historyOut-of-sample improvement over simple rules

notes: No AI, IoT, ERP integration or predictive model is claimed as implemented. Start with rule-based monitoring. Payback calculations require measured baseline costs and downtime.

title: Implementation sequence and decision gates
subtitle: Suggested phases; timing depends on team capacity
body:
01

Harden foundations

Permissions · schemas · transactions · truthful costing

02

Complete QR & PPM

Four choices · versioned checklists · controlled transfers

03

Automate operations

Background alerts · outbox retries · reconciliation · mobile pilot

04

Extend and optimize

Indexes / pagination · ERP pilot · sensors · predictive feasibility

Gate each phase with role-based acceptance tests and a pilot in one unit before expanding.
source: Proposed sequencing; no approved budget or delivery dates
notes: Phase 1: reject unauthorized transitions and test concurrent stock updates. Phase 2: persist all check results and transfer receipt. Phase 3: test closed-browser escalation and offline conflicts. Phase 4: show measured integration or sensor outcomes.

title: Measure outcomes without inventing results
subtitle: Establish a baseline before claiming improvement
body:
MeasureDefinitionRequired data
Repair duration / MTTRCompleted repair duration ÷ completed repairsConsistent start / resolution timestamps
PPM on-time completionCompleted by due date ÷ tasks dueHistorical due dates and completion events
Stockout frequencyBlocked material requests ÷ material requestsIssue ledger and unfulfilled quantities
Repeat failuresSame machine / fault in a defined windowNormalized faults and ticket links
Availability / MTBFUse planned time and operating exposureProduction / runtime data, not ticket counts alone
notes: Separate repair work time from production downtime. T&A report-to-resolution duration can include waiting. Targets need a baseline and operations agreement; no percentage improvements are asserted.

title: What this review establishes
subtitle: Source inspection and local checks, with explicit limits
body:
Review coverage

  • Routes, dashboards and shared types
  • Authentication and database resolution
  • Repair, service, PPM and stock flows
  • Reminders, imports and reporting helpers

Limits

  • No customer data or production audit
  • No live role-by-role acceptance test
  • No measured uptime, savings or fleet totals
  • Source does not establish deployment status

See accompanying analysis notes for the local regression results.
notes: Uncommitted changes are included. Source takes precedence where README and handover descriptions differ. HTML presentation checks are separate from application validation.

title: The next milestone
subtitle: Complete a reliable maintenance cycle in one pilot unit
body:
Scan the machine.
Record the work.
Trust the result.

Recommended pilot scope

Four QR actions, structured PPM checks, controlled transfers and transaction-safe repair / stock changes.

Review before rollout

Operations signs off workflows. Stores validates quantities. Supervisors verify history. Engineering proves access and retries.

PROPOSED NEXT MILESTONE
source: Synthesis of source review and implementation roadmap
notes: Suggested decision: agree on pilot scope and name an operations owner. This presentation does not implement the proposed application features.
